findings.claim: The longer-phrase filter can erase a valid bank return code before the code gets its required precedence.
findings.repro: Add UNPAID DD TO SAVINGS to the existing own_pots_savings names list and load v2. Classify a £50 credit described as UNPAID DD TO SAVINGS. The longer own-account rule removes the anchored returned_dd match and the credit becomes an own-account transfer. R4 requires the bank code at the start to settle it as a returned payment.

findings.claim: The span scan still loses longer alternatives inside a single regex. The passing regression at tests/test_rules_v2.py:1656 exercises a short regex and a separate longer name.
findings.repro: In that regression, put both alternatives in the acme rule's pattern as \bACME\b|\bACME FASTER PAYMENT LTD\b, remove names, and keep the FASTER PAYMENT rail. On a £100 ACME FASTER PAYMENT LTD CASH DEPOSIT credit, also include the shipped cash_paid_in rule. The short regex alternative wins at the shared start, so the rail survives and produces an ambiguity. The longer phrase should suppress the embedded rail, leaving two trading-receipt matches that agree on the bucket.

findings.claim: The README's returned-DD linking claim exceeds the v2 implementation. Newly recognised returned-payment wording stays in the payee used for reversal matching.
findings.repro: Categorise a £450 DD IWOCA LTD debit followed by a £450 RETURNED DD IWOCA LTD credit. The credit gets v2:returned_payment but has no reverses id because the normalized names differ. The passing test at tests/test_rules_v2.py:549 uses UNPAID DD instead.

findings.claim: The documented precedence contradicts the implementation and R4. It says a profile name settles an ambiguous credit and omits the cheque cue and own-account pairing.
findings.repro: Compare the README row with classification of FPS CREDIT CASH DEPOSIT REF JANE DOE with Jane Doe in the director profile. The credit remains ambiguous and the profile name adds a candidate. CHEQUE CASH DEPOSIT likewise remains ambiguous.

findings.claim: The reported 0.69-second result is unverified by the runner. The full log proves the under-two-second assertion passed for the categoriser workload.
findings.repro: Find test_categorise_10000_lines_under_v2_with_a_profile_is_fast in specified-3.log. It reports PASSED without the elapsed time of the measured section. Run python -m pytest -q tests/test_rules_v2.py -k 10000_lines with that section's elapsed time emitted to verify the specific figure.

findings.claim: The compile claim for src, evals and tests is only partly covered by the configured compile gate. The suite and marker counts in the claim are stale.
findings.repro: Compare the claim with mechanical:2, which ran python -m compileall -q src. The command covering the full claimed scope is python -m compileall -q src evals tests. The passed runner totals are 732 full-suite, 110 contracts, 138 invariants and 83 dual-run. Both offline ruleset eval tests passed in specified-3.log.
